terms.gloss: a noun for something that can be seen and touched
evidence: Quint. 1.4.20 (Lewis & Short s.v. vocābulum, as a common noun against nōmen); the words ut esset vocābulum corpus vīsū tāctūque manifestum, domus, lectus not checked
terms.comment: The other half of the division Quintilian reports (see abstract noun). Elsewhere vocābulum is any common noun, or any word (see noun, word).

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 245, p. 247.
Quintilian checked against the Perseus Latin texts, and cited by its numbering.
